ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $5.00 cancellation fee; no refund and no account flag. Send the rider a brief note pointing to the driver's recorded arrival and 8-minute wait window.
ruling.reasoning:
Entry is through NS-0: the record shows cancelled_by = driver and the driver's stated reason is rider no-show, so the $5.00 charged is tested against NS-1 / NS-2 [F4][RD-6 NS-0]. (RD-6 is not the clause applied here; the entry clause is NS-0.)

The case record carries its own threshold: the trace fixes the no-show threshold at 8 minutes (at least) for this case, and NS-1 says that when the case record carries a threshold, (iii) is executed on that record's threshold rather than the 3-minute default [F6][NS-1]. The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:17:10, 39 m from the pickup point at that moment — inside the 200 m data-layer radius used by NS-1(ii) — so NS-1(i) and (ii) are met [F6][F1][NS-1]. After that tap he remained continuously within 200 m for 8 min 10 s and was stationary 41 m from the pickup from 12:16:50 until the 12:25:20 cancellation, i.e. 490 s of recorded continuous presence against the 480 s threshold; the GPS/timeline samples bracket the whole wait with no gap, so the continuity element is settled by the record and no manual review under NS-1's integrity proviso is triggered [F6][F3][F4][F5][F2][NS-1].

The rider's complaint is that he was still inside when the driver cancelled, and the chat shows the driver announcing arrival at 12:17 and then cancelling at 12:25 with no further contact [F9][F10][F11][F4]. Reading the messages, none asks or refuses anything, and the log is complete and fully timestamped, so nothing in the record supports a finding that the rider appeared or contacted the driver during the wait; the system records of arrival, location and continuous wait override the unrecorded narrative in the complaint [F3][F5][F6][NS-1].

Because every element of NS-1 is recorded as met, NS-2 — which is conditional on any of (i)(ii)(iii) failing — is not triggered and the $5.00 stands [F7][F4][NS-1][NS-2]. The $5.00 figure is the amount on the fare record; the trace instructs that the case record's $5.00 and its 8-minute threshold be read wherever NS-1/NS-2 name $6.61 and 3 minutes, so there is no item to refund and the amount is nil [F7][F4][NS-1]. The driver's surplus "8 minutes the rule gives" statement is not relied on [F12][NS-1]; NS-7 (30-day dispute window, voucher form) never arises because nothing is refundable [F4][NS-7].

Account flag: the driver's profile (2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 d) could only ever be an add-on, and RD-6 requires the case to be established first — here the charge is upheld, so no flag arises on this case [F17][RD-6]. The driver's admission that he was 41 m from the door rather than at it does not fail NS-1(ii), which is measured at the moment of the arrival confirmation [F3][F6][NS-1].

rejected_claims.reason: Entry via NS-0 is correct, but the charge satisfies NS-1 on the case record's own 8-minute threshold (F6: 490 s inside 200 m after the tap), so no refund arises under NS-2 [F4][F6][NS-1][NS-2].

The premise that no case-record threshold exists is wrong: the trace fixes the no-show threshold at 8 min for this case, and NS-1 executes (iii) on the record's threshold where one is carried [F6][NS-1].
Withdrawn by the rider, and in any event the continuous-wait element is settled by the record: 8 min 10 s inside 200 m after the tap, stationary until the 12:25:20 cancellation [F6][F3][NS-1].
The complaint narrative is a statement without a system record behind it, while the GPS/timeline show a stationary car 41 m from the pickup through to cancellation [F3][F4][NS-1].
NS-2 is conditional on NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) failing; each element is recorded as met, so the $5.00 charge stands [F6][F7][NS-1][NS-2].
Profile facts cannot decide a case; the rider's clean record does not displace the recorded wait [F16][NS-1].

The driver's conclusion is upheld, but not on the two grounds pleaded together: the $5.00 item is the no-show cancellation fee on the fare record, and it stands under NS-1; NS-6 (post-wait boarding plus completed trip) is not needed and is not applicable to a trip cancelled before boarding [F4][F7][NS-1].
The driver's self-declared '8 minutes the rule gives' is surplusage and is not relied on; the wait is established by the system record, not by his statement [F12][F6][NS-1].
